+# Prime roots on complete return-chart families
+
+## Abstract
+
+Prime cardinality turns component routing into an exact local-or-cyclic root criterion.
+
+Let p be any prime natural number, H any group, X:Fin p->Type an arbitrary dependent family, and A_i:ReturnAtlas H (X i) complete signed return charts. Write d_i>0 for their atlas periods and h_i for their holonomies. DependentReturnAtlases(H,X) denotes precisely this dependent family of charts, and Sigma(X) is the entire disjoint carrier of pairs (i,x) with x:X i. The chart equality is A_i(t,z)=A_i(s,w) exactly when t=s+d_i*m and z*h_i^m=w for some integer m. The group may be infinite and noncommutative. The d_i are primitive-base return periods, not ordinary minimal periods of the lifted time maps.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Time on the dependent union).**
+
+$$\forall H \in Type,\; [\operatorname{Group}\left(H\right)]\forall J \in Type, X \in \operatorname{Map}\left(J, Type\right), A \in \operatorname{DependentReturnAtlases}\left(H, X\right),\; \forall q \in \operatorname{Sigma}\left(X\right),\; \operatorname{apply}\left(\operatorname{jointTime}\left(A\right), q\right) = \operatorname{pair}\left(\operatorname{first}\left(q\right), \operatorname{time}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, \operatorname{first}\left(q\right)\right), \operatorname{second}\left(q\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/PrimeOrbitRootCriterion.jointTime` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary index type J and a family A_j, the time map T sends (i,x) to (i,A_i.time(x)). Every point of every chart remains in the carrier.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Left deck action on the dependent union).**
+
+$$\forall H \in Type,\; [\operatorname{Group}\left(H\right)]\forall J \in Type, X \in \operatorname{Map}\left(J, Type\right), A \in \operatorname{DependentReturnAtlases}\left(H, X\right),\; \forall a \in H, q \in \operatorname{Sigma}\left(X\right),\; \operatorname{apply}\left(\operatorname{jointDeck}\left(A, a\right), q\right) = \operatorname{pair}\left(\operatorname{first}\left(q\right), \operatorname{deck}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, \operatorname{first}\left(q\right)\right), a, \operatorname{second}\left(q\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/PrimeOrbitRootCriterion.jointDeck` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary index type J and a:H the deck map D_a sends (i,x) to (i,A_i.deck(a,x)). It uses the same left group element in each component; signed return holonomy still multiplies on the right.
+

+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/PrimeOrbitRootCriterion.Local` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*

((\operatorname{period}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, i\right)\right) = \operatorname{period}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, j\right)\right)) \land (\exists b \in H,\; \operatorname{mul}\left(b, \operatorname{holonomy}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, j\right)\right)\right) = \operatorname{mul}\left(\operatorname{holonomy}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(A, i\right)\right), b\right)))))))$$
+

+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+There exists a map R:Sigma X->Sigma X with R(D_a(q))=D_a(R(q)) for every a and q, and R iterated p times equal to T, if and only if either every A_i satisfies Local p A_i or for every i,j one has d_i=d_j and some b:H with b*h_j=h_i*b. The two alternatives may overlap. R is not assumed to preserve charts, be bijective, or commute with time.
+
+Necessity first derives time commutation from R^p=T and injectivity from the injectivity of T. Completeness of each chart makes the target component of R(i,x) independent of x: deck moves cover its group coordinate, and nonnegative time moves cover its normalized finite phase. This induces sigma:Fin p->Fin p with sigma^p=id. Each restricted map between routed components is injective and intertwines deck and time. Apply ReturnAtlasFiniteCovers.normal_form and its actual fiberEquiv: a positive degree m gives Fin m equivalent to the full preimage of every target point. Injectivity forces any two such preimages equal; if m>1 the images of 0 and 1 contradict injectivity of that equivalence. Hence m=1, yielding equal atlas periods and b*h_j=h_i*b without counting H.
+
+If sigma fixes every index, restriction gives an actual pth root in each chart, and the existing local root criterion gives all local equations. Otherwise choose a nonfixed index o. Mathlib's prime minimal-period theorem gives minimalPeriod(sigma,o)=p. Its p distinct iterates exhaust Fin p. Apply the same injective-factor argument to every iterate of R to identify A_o with every chart. Inverting and composing the resulting conjugacies gives the displayed condition for every ordered pair i,j. No fixed-order enumeration is used.
+
+For sufficiency, local roots combine directly on the dependent union. In the other case choose gauges b_i with b_i*h_i=h_o*b_i and equal periods. Existing complete-coordinate transport identifies the entire union with Fin p times X_o, by (i,x)->(i,transport(A_i,A_o,b_i inverse,x)). In these coordinates define C(i,y)=((i.val+1) mod p, T_o^floor((i.val+1)/p)(y)). Induction proves C^n(i,y)=((i.val+n) mod p, T_o^floor((i.val+n)/p)(y)). Thus C^p(i,y)=(i,T_o(y)); exactly one time step occurs at the wrap. Deck commutation of T_o makes C deck equivariant. Conjugating C back through the full chart equivalence constructs the required actual map R.
+
+This connects cyclic permutation arithmetic, the signed finite-cover degree, and nonabelian holonomy conjugacy. The restriction to exactly p charts makes a single nonfixed prime orbit fill the entire index set. Larger finite families require additional orbit multiplicity information; no criterion for those families is asserted here. These arguments combine established permutation and return-chart mechanisms, with no claim of literature priority.

+

+
+The primitive-base period ratio is the exact degree of an intertwining map, even for infinite noncommutative deck groups.

+# Finite families and exact root multiplicities
+
+## Abstract
+
+Allowed component cycles give an exact additive criterion for equivariant roots on any finite chart family.
+
+Let H be any group, iota any finite type, X:iota->Type any dependent family, and A_i:ReturnAtlas H (X i) complete signed return charts. No finiteness or commutativity is required of H. The finite index type may be empty. Write d_i>0 for the atlas period and h_i for the holonomy. Each chart covers its entire carrier and satisfies A_i(t,z)=A_i(s,w) exactly when t=s+d_i*m and z*h_i^m=w for some integer m. These periods describe the primitive base returns, rather than the ordinary periods of the lifted time maps.
+
+On Sigma X, T(i,x)=(i,A_i.time(x)) and D_a(i,x)=(i,A_i.deck(a,x)) are the existing jointTime and jointDeck. Isotypic A i j means d_i=d_j and there exists b:H with b*h_j=h_i*b. It is an equivalence relation, expressing equal periods and conjugate holonomy. IsotypicClass(A,i) denotes the subtype {j:iota | Isotypic A i j}, and NatCard is its finite cardinality. Local q B is the existing signed local equation: there exist s:Fin B.period, m:Int and b:H with b commuting with B.holonomy, q*s.val=1+B.period*m, and b^q*B.holonomy^m=1. The integer m is unrestricted in sign.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Exact additive multiplicity criterion).**
+
+$$\forall H \in Type,\; [\operatorname{Group}\left(H\right)]\forall iota \in Type, X \in \operatorname{Map}\left(iota, Type\right), A \in \operatorname{DependentReturnAtlases}\left(H, X\right),\; [\operatorname{Finite}\left(iota\right)]\forall k \in Nat,\; 0 < k \implies ((\exists R \in \operatorname{Map}\left(\operatorname{Sigma}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Sigma}\left(X\right)\right),\; ((\forall a \in H, x \in \operatorname{Sigma}\left(X\right),\; \operatorname{apply}\left(R, \operatorname{apply}\left(\operatorname{jointDeck}\left(A, a\right), x\right)\right) = \operatorname{apply}\left(\operatorname{jointDeck}\left(A, a\right), \operatorname{apply}\left(R, x\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{iterate}\left(R, k\right) = \operatorname{jointTime}\left(A\right)))) \iff (\forall i \in iota,\; \exists L \in \operatorname{List}\left(Nat\right),\; ((\operatorname{sum}\left(L\right) = \operatorname{NatCard}\left(\operatorname{IsotypicClass}\left(A, i\right)\right)) \land (\forall ell \in Nat,\; \operatorname{Mem}\left(ell, L\right) \implies ((0 < ell) \land (((\operatorname{Divides}\left(ell, k\right)) \land (\operatorname{Local}\left(\operatorname{natDiv}\left(k, ell\right), \operatorname{apply}\left(A, i\right)\right)))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/FiniteOrbitRootCriterion.finite_root_criterion` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.

+*Commentary.*
+
+For every positive natural k, an unrestricted map R:Sigma X->Sigma X with R(D_a(x))=D_a(R(x)) for all a,x and R iterated k times equal to T exists if and only if, for every index i, there is an actual finite list L of natural block lengths whose sum is the cardinality of {j | Isotypic A i j}, and each ell in L is positive, divides k, and satisfies Local (k/ell) A_i. Gauges built from the existing complete coordinates and right multiplication identify every chart in that block with the representative chart. The theorem keeps the actual list of lengths. It extends the earlier two-chart, three-chart and prime-cardinality mechanisms by retaining all component-cycle multiplicities. No literature priority is claimed.

+# Rational time on a single complete return chart
+
+## Abstract
+
+One complete return chart supports rational time precisely when its phase period is one and its holonomy extends to a rational group homomorphism.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Exact criterion for a coherent rational action).**
+
+$$\forall u \in Universe, v \in Universe,\; \forall H \in \operatorname{Type}\left(u\right),\; [\operatorname{Group}\left(H\right)]\forall X \in \operatorname{Type}\left(v\right), A \in \operatorname{ReturnAtlas}\left(H, X\right),\; ((\exists rho \in \operatorname{MonoidHom}\left(\operatorname{Multiplicative}\left(Rational\right), \operatorname{Perm}\left(X\right)\right),\; ((\forall q \in \operatorname{Multiplicative}\left(Rational\right),\; \operatorname{Equivariant}\left(A, \operatorname{apply}\left(rho, q\right)\right)) \land \operatorname{underlyingFunction}\left(\operatorname{apply}\left(rho, \operatorname{ofAdd}\left(1\right)\right)\right) = \operatorname{time}\left(A\right))) \iff (\operatorname{period}\left(A\right) = 1 \land \exists phi \in \operatorname{MonoidHom}\left(\operatorname{Multiplicative}\left(Rational\right), H\right),\; \operatorname{apply}\left(phi, \operatorname{ofAdd}\left(1\right)\right) = \operatorname{holonomy}\left(A\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/RationalReturnAtlasCriterion.rational_time_action_criterion` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The universes u and v are independent. H is any group, X is any carrier, and A is a complete signed ReturnAtlas H X. A has a positive natural period d, holonomy h in H, and coordinates point(t,z). Its complete equality relation is point(t,z)=point(s,w) exactly when t=s+d*m and z*h^m=w for some integer m. Its time map advances t by one, while deck(a) multiplies z on the left. These are the entire hypotheses; H may be infinite, noncommutative or have torsion.
+
+Multiplicative Rational is the additive group of all rational numbers written multiplicatively. Its identity is ofAdd(0); ofAdd(1) is the positive unit time. A monoid homomorphism rho into Perm X is one coherent action, with rho(ofAdd(q+r))=rho(ofAdd(q))*rho(ofAdd(r)) and rho(ofAdd(0)) the identity permutation. Equivariant A (rho(q)) means that rho(q)(deck(a,x))=deck(a,rho(q)(x)) for every a in H and x in X. The displayed equality at unit time is equality of the underlying functions on all X. Neither continuity nor an order or topology is assumed.
+
+For necessity, put R=rho(ofAdd(1/d)). The homomorphism law gives R^d=rho(ofAdd(1)), hence the dth iterate of R is A.time. Apply the existing ReturnAtlas.root_criterion at k=d. Its signed equation is d*s.val=1+d*m, so d divides 1 and d=1. This uses the existing signed root classification rather than a separate classification of roots.
+
+When d=1, the existing complete atlas coordinates give the equivalence e:H equiv X defined by e(z)=point(0,z). The left deck law becomes e(a*z)=deck(a,e(z)); the signed return relation gives time(e(z))=e(z*h). Every deck-equivariant permutation rho(q) therefore has the form rho(q)(e(z))=e(z*b(q)), where b(q)=e inverse(rho(q)(e(1))). With permutation multiplication interpreted as composition, right translations satisfy R(b)*R(c)=R(c*b). Consequently the immediate composition rule is b(p*q)=b(q)*b(p). Commutativity of the rational source also gives b(p*q)=b(p)*b(q), producing the required genuine homomorphism phi into H. Unit time forces phi(ofAdd(1))=h.
+
+Conversely, a homomorphism phi with this unit value defines rho(q) by transporting z maps to z*phi(q) through e. The images of phi commute because the rational source is commutative, so these right translations satisfy the permutation homomorphism law in its actual composition order. Associativity makes them commute with every left deck translation, and the value at ofAdd(1) is exactly time. The construction includes zero and negative rational times and uses neither finite nor countable carriers nor a divisibility hypothesis on H.

+has no nonzero element annihilated by one fixed natural number greater than one.
+The target group need not be commutative or have continuous group operations. -/
+theorem continuous_addHom_injective_or_eq_zero
+    {K : Type u} [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K]
+    [TopologicalSpace K] [OrderTopology K] [Archimedean K]
+    {A : Type v} [AddGroup A] [TopologicalSpace A] [T1Space A]
+    (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 < p) (hpt : ∀ x : A, p • x = 0 → x = 0)
+    (f : K →+ A) (hf : Continuous f) : Function.Injective f ∨ f = 0 := by
+  by_cases hbot : f.ker = ⊥
+  · exact Or.inl (f.ker_eq_bot_iff.mp hbot)
+  right
+  have hpK : (1 : K) < p := by exact_mod_cast hp
+  have hp0 : (0 : K) < p := zero_lt_one.trans hpK
+  have hdense : Dense (f.ker : Set K) := by
+    apply f.ker.dense_of_no_min hbot
+    rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
+    have hb : a / (p : K) ∈ f.ker := by
+      change f (a / (p : K)) = 0
+      apply hpt
+      rw [← map_nsmul]
+      have hdiv : p • (a / (p : K)) = a := by
+        rw [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_div_cancel₀ _ (ne_of_gt hp0)]
+      rw [hdiv]
+      exact ha.1.1
+    exact (not_le_of_gt (div_lt_self ha.1.2 hpK))
+      (ha.2 ⟨hb, div_pos ha.1.2 hp0⟩)
+  have hclosed : IsClosed (f.ker : Set K) :=
+    isClosed_singleton.preimage hf
+  apply AddMonoidHom.ker_eq_top_iff.mp
+  apply SetLike.coe_injective
+  change (f.ker : Set K) = Set.univ
+  rw [← hclosed.closure_eq, hdense.closure_eq]
+
+#print axioms continuous_addHom_injective_or_eq_zero
+
